Venezuela possesses some of the world’s most significant natural resources, which helps explain why it has long attracted international geopolitical interest, including from the United States during Donald Trump’s presidency. Most notably, Venezuela has the largest proven oil reserves in the world, primarily located in the Orinoco Belt. Oil has historically been the backbone of Venezuela’s economy, accounting for the vast majority of export revenues. Because oil is central to global energy markets, countries with large reserves are strategically important, especially during periods of energy insecurity or price volatility.In addition to oil, Venezuela has substantial natural gas reserves, making it one of the most resource-rich energy producers in the Western Hemisphere. While much of this gas remains underdeveloped due to infrastructure and economic constraints, it represents long-term strategic value for energy production and export. Venezuela also has extensive mineral wealth, including gold, iron ore, bauxite (used to produce aluminum), and deposits of copper, nickel, and diamonds. Of particular strategic interest are rare earth elements and coltan, which are critical for modern technologies such as electronics, renewable energy systems, and military equipment.These resources are concentrated in areas such as the Orinoco Mining Arc, a region believed to contain vast untapped mineral deposits. Beyond raw materials, Venezuela also has major hydroelectric capacity, including one of the largest dams in the world, which historically supplied much of the country’s electricity and could support large-scale industrial activity. Taken together, this combination of energy resources, critical minerals, and geographic proximity to the United States makes Venezuela strategically significant.However, it is important to distinguish strategic interest from legal justification for military action. Under international law, Venezuela has full sovereignty over its natural resources, and there is no lawful basis for another country to attack it simply to gain access to those resources. Official U.S. policy under Donald Trump publicly framed pressure on Venezuela around issues such as governance, human rights, sanctions enforcement, drug trafficking, and regional security. While analysts often argue that Venezuela’s resource wealth forms part of the broader geopolitical background, it has never been formally cited as a legal or official reason for military intervention.
